steps.body: A tiny square and a giant square share one name, because they share what matters: four equal sides, four corners.
steps.narration: A tiny square and a giant square share one name, because they share what matters: four equal sides, four corners.

widget.prompt: Measure the large square's side. Start at zero and cover it with 6 equal unit blocks.
widget.successFeedback: 6 equal blocks cover the large square's side exactly. It is bigger, but it is still a square.
widget.alignFeedback: Line up zero with the object's starting end before measuring.
widget.gapOverlapFeedback: The blocks must touch end to end — no spaces and no covering the same part twice.
widget.unitFeedback: Every block must be the same size, or the count means nothing.

predict.prompt: A square grows to double size. What happens to its name?
predict.reveal: Growing stretches the sides but keeps four-equal-and-four-corners — the name rides on those.

cml.actionGoal: Name shapes by sides and corners, place them with position words, and compose them edge to edge for kgb size invariance.
invariants: A shape's name lives in its sides and corners — not its size, pose, or color; position words compare a thing to a landmark; and shapes joined edge to edge compose a larger whole — the anchors for kgb size invariance.
misconceptions: Renaming a turned or resized shape, using position words without a landmark, or treating shapes as unjoinable.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If the shape were turned upside down, which of its sides or corners would disappear?

options.feedback: Yes. Size can change, but 4 equal sides and 4 corners still make a square.

options.label: Only the big one is a square
options.feedback: The small shape has the same 4 equal sides and 4 corners, so it is a square too.

options.feedback: The big shape has the same 4 equal sides and 4 corners, so it is a square too.

options.label: They must be the same size

widget.prompt: A square grows bigger, but its sides and corners stay the same. What stays true?

options.label: It is still a square
options.feedback: Yes. Growing changes size, not the 4 equal sides and 4 corners that make a square.

options.label: It becomes a rectangle
options.feedback: Its 4 sides are still equal, so its square name stays.

options.label: It becomes a triangle
options.feedback: A triangle needs 3 sides. This shape still has 4.

options.label: It has no shape name
options.feedback: Big or small, a closed shape keeps its name when its defining parts stay the same.

widget.prompt: Start at 3. Hop once for each of a square's 4 corners. Where do you land?

commonLandings.feedback: That stops one complete hop too soon. Continue the final 1-unit hop to reach 7.
That goes one complete hop too far. Count exactly 4 hops from 3.

widget.missFeedback: Count 4 on from 3: you land on 7.
widget.successFeedback: 7 — each corner takes one hop, and the landing is the count.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — all 4 counts are needed to reach 7.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — the count stops after 4 hops, on 7.

options.label: Still a square

options.feedback: The sides and corners keep their equal-and-4 rule as it grows; nothing that names the shape changed.
